title: Rare-earth oxysulfides RE$_2$O$_2$S as model mixed-anion frustrated magnets
authors: Austin M. Ferrenti, Ksenia Khoroshun, Mohamed Oudah, Graham King, Jonathan Gaudet, Alannah M. Hallas
abstract: The study of low-dimensional and anisotropic magnetism is a promising avenue for the discovery of novel quantum phenomena. Mixed-anion materials, defined by the coordination of metal cations by two or more distinct anionic species, provide an intrinsically anisotropic platform for the tuning of structural, magnetic, and electronic properties. In this work, we report the synthesis and characterization of a family of rare-earth oxysulfide (RE$_2$O$_2$S) antiferromagnets (AFM) possessing a triangular-bilayer slab lattice geometry. Long-range AFM order is observed for the majority of compositions, with several (RE = Ce, Pr, Nd, Sm) having been previously unreported. Although assumed to form stoichiometrically, pair distribution function (PDF) analysis provides evidence for significant, synthesis-dependent interslab structural disorder as RE$_2$O$_{2+x}$S$_{1-x}$, resulting in significant variability in the bulk magnetic response of the Nd member. This work highlights the tunability of frustrated magnetic ground states in rare-earth-based mixed-anion materials, and the importance of thorough structural characterization in the discovery of new mixed-anion magnets.
summary: This work reports on rare-earth oxysulfides ($	ext{RE}_2	ext{O}_2	ext{S}$), which are mixed-anion magnets with a quasi-2D slab structure. By synthesizing and characterizing these materials, the authors demonstrate that the mixed-anion character allows for the tuning of magnetic frustration. The combination of structural analysis and magnetic measurements confirms the existence of tunable, anisotropic magnetic ground states.
main_problem: The study investigates the tunability of frustrated magnetic ground states in rare-earth mixed-anion materials.
main_result: The $	ext{RE}_2	ext{O}_2	ext{S}$ compounds exhibit long-range antiferromagnetic order and show tunable magnetic frustration due to their quasi-2D, mixed-anion structure.
method: The study combines synthesis, structural characterization (pXRD, PDF analysis), and magnetic measurements ($\chi(T)$, $M(H)$) with theoretical modeling (CEF calculations).
model_or_system: The physical system is the rare-earth oxysulfide ($	ext{RE}_2	ext{O}_2	ext{S}$), which forms a triangular-bilayer slab lattice geometry, acting as an intermediate between 3D oxides and 2D delafossites.
key_observables: Long-range AFM order, metamagnetic transitions, lattice parameters ($a, c$), and magnetic susceptibility ($\mu_{	ext{eff}}, 	heta_{	ext{CW}}$).
important_parameters: The rare-earth element (RE) identity, the degree of structural disorder ($x$ in $	ext{RE}_2	ext{O}_{2+x}	ext{S}_{1-x}$), and temperature ($T_N$).
main_assumptions: The structural disorder observed via PDF analysis is attributed to synthesis-dependent oxygen/sulfur mixing, and average structural changes are assumed representative across the RE series.
figures_summary: Figures show crystal structures, pXRD refinements tracking lattice parameter changes with RE size, and PDF data illustrating structural disorder across different samples.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from structural characterization (pXRD, PDF) to magnetic measurements ($\chi(T)$, $M(H)$), establishing the structural basis for the observed magnetic frustration and tunability.
why_interesting: The interplay between structural disorder (mixed anions) and magnetic frustration in quasi-2D systems is a rich area for theoretical modeling, potentially involving spin liquid physics or complex exchange Hamiltonians.
